_readme: Every playable character. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. id is written into save files, so never rename one after a save exists; role and attackType are matched case-insensitively against CharacterRole and DamageType, and CharacterEntryResolver rejects an unknown name at build time rather than shipping a character that silently falls through to the wrong Skill case. THE SIX ABILITY SCORES NO LONGER FOLLOW A FIXED BUDGET. Through 2026-09-07 every character's six scores had to total exactly 60, so differentiation was redistribution rather than growth: a new character could not be quietly stronger than the roster by being above average at everything, because to be tough somewhere it had to be feeble somewhere else. The owner dropped that rule on 2026-09-07 and shipped Shawn/Bjorn/Odette at totals of 66/64/62 as written, on the reasoning that the three authored spreads read fine without it; CharacterEntryResolver and ContentDatabase.ValidateContent no longer refuse an off-total row. If a future character turns out to be a flatly stronger pick than the roster for having no real weakness, that is the failure mode the budget existed to prevent, and reinstating `total == AbilityScoreBudget` in both places (the constant is gone; it was 60, six times the neutral score) is the fix. Each score still has to be a plausible number on its own — refused below 1 or above 30 in the resolver, and outside 3-20 in the built-catalogue check. STAT SPREADS EXPRESS THE ROLE, so a squad's strengths are readable from its species alone, and attackType gives each character an elemental identity for the weakness/resistance system: five characters cover five of the six DamageType values, chosen by loose theme (wool/pasture, sting, bite, cold-blooded shell, old and wise) rather than min-maxed against the enemy roster. BOTH ART PATHS ARE RESOURCES-RELATIVE AND CARRY NO EXTENSION: portraitPath names one head-and-shoulders PNG under Resources/Portraits/ (the dossier plate) and battleSpritePath a folder of full-body stance art (the fight stage, produced by tools/slice_actor_sheet.py). Both load at runtime, so a row added here is complete the moment the content is rebuilt. portraitPath was ASSETS-relative and baked into the scene until 2026-09-06, which meant a character authored between scene builds had a correct name, correct attributes and an empty portrait plate that no content rebuild could fill; the two conventions still coexist elsewhere in content (iconPath, iconSheet are baked), and ArtPathConvention is the one statement of which field is which. owl still wears Shawn's face (Portraits/sheep) until her own portrait is drawn. SIGNATURE RESOURCES are each character's own private combat resource; an EMPTY signatureId means the character has none — that is the meaningful distinction, not a zero capacity. WHICH POOL A CHARACTER'S SKILLS SPEND IS ALSO CONTENT: primaryPoolId names a row in pools.json and blank means mana, so trading mana for a different resource — a different capacity rule, different gains, different colours, and no spell books — is one field on this row rather than a special case in code (Bjorn's is `fury`). All five ride the same three triggers (per-turn, on-attack, on-damage-taken), so a new one is content and wiring rather than a parallel system; what makes them feel different is WHICH trigger dominates. Wool (Shawn) is the balanced template: attack-led with a real per-turn and damage-taken floor, and it is armour and ammunition out of one pool — incoming damage eats it before his health and his abilities shear it off, so every turn is bank-or-spend and both answers are real. His plain Attack pays the most because his Attack is 5 against enemy Defense of up to 9, i.e. nearly worthless as damage; giving it the best Wool yield turns his weakest action into a deliberate choice. He starts every fight at zero, which is why he has the worst opening turn in the game and the best closing one. Venom (Fly) is attack-led and nothing else: fast and fragile, so rewarding getting hit would be a trap. Fangs (Dog) is per-turn and damage-taken roughly even — a patient hunter also provoked by pain. Shell (Turtle) is damage-taken-led by a wide margin on the highest capacity of the five: the literal tank converts punishment into its own resource. Insight (Owl) is per-turn-led and almost nothing else: a passive scholarly resource fitting a backline Support who is often neither attacking nor being hit. ALL THREE STARTING SPREADS ARE AUTHORED NOW, as of 2026-09-07: Shawn (STR 12, DEX 10, CON 14, WIS 12, INT 8, CHA 10 — total 66), Bjorn (STR 12, DEX 12, CON 14, WIS 8, INT 8, CHA 10 — total 64) and Odette (STR 8, DEX 12, CON 8, WIS 12, INT 14, CHA 8 — total 62), each shipped as written on the owner's call rather than trimmed back onto the old 60 budget (see the ability-score paragraph above). baseStats (maxHealth, speed, attack, physicalDefense, magicalDefense) were left untouched by that change on purpose — the point of moving abilities without touching baseStats is that a character's EFFECTIVE stats (Health, Attack, Speed, Mana Regen, both DEF lines, Max Mana) move on their own, purely through AbilityDerivation, with nothing hand-tuned to compensate. ROSTER ORDER IS FILE ORDER: sortOrder is assigned from position here, because Resources.LoadAll returns filename order and that silently reshuffles which characters land in the default squad (CLAUDE.md gotcha 4). Turtle is the fourth slot and the first to actually need extra_recruit_slot for a full squad to reach it; Owl is the fifth and completes the five CharacterRole values. plateTheme is the character's IDENTITY COLOUR, worn by the rim and the name of every fight-HUD card that stands for them (Domain.UiKit.PcTheme maps the theme to its two hexes); matched case-insensitively against UiKit.ButtonTheme and REQUIRED on every row -- an empty or unknown value refuses the build, because every valid value is some other character's colour. Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md.
